CONFIRM C0106 — `verify_bundle()` delegates to `VerificationChain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)` but never checks that the bundled record’s `chain_hash` matches `proof["chain_hash"]`. In `verification_chain.py`, proof verification uses only `proof["chain_hash"]`, `proof["proof"]`, and the root; the exported `record` is otherwise ignored. A tampered bundle can pair a valid proof with a different record and still verify. FOLLOW: this breaks the core “self-contained bundle” contract because external audit can accept corrupted record contents as included. The same mismatch also makes per-record error messages misleading because `seq` comes from `record` while validation came from `proof`. Existing fix direction is sufficient: compare `record["chain_hash"]` to `proof["chain_hash"]` before verification and fail on mismatch.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()` silently ignores extra bundled records or extra proofs because it iterates with `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)`. Location: `verify_bundle`, loop `for i, (record, proof) in enumerate(zip(...))`. Evidence: Python `zip` truncates to the shorter input. If a bundle has 3 records and 2 proofs, only the first 2 pairs are checked and the method can return success with one unverified record. If it has 2 records and 3 proofs, one proof is ignored. This violates the stated contract “verify all inclusion proofs in a bundle.”
FOLLOW: The bug affects any consumer relying on `verify_bundle()` as a completeness check for exported bundles. A malformed or tampered bundle can pass verification while omitting proofs for some records, so downstream provenance/audit tooling may treat partial bundles as fully verified. It compounds C0106: even if record/proof binding is fixed, unmatched tails are still unchecked.
